body.p: I. Introduction

The undersigned thanks Examiner Yankey for review and consideration of the present Application. In response to the Office Action of October 27, 2023 ("Office Action"), the undersigned submits the present amendment and remarks ("Response").

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 24-40 will be pending in this application. Claims 24, 38, and 39 have been amended, and claim 41 has been cancelled. Claims 1-23 were previously cancelled. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims. II. Drawing Objections

The drawings are objected to for failing to show a "privacy screen" as recited in claim 21. Applicant believes the Office Action intended to refer to claim 39, but in any event submits that the objection is moot because a "privacy screen" is no longer recited in any claim. III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 112

Claim 39 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention. In view of the amendments to claim 39, Applicant submits that the claim particularly points out and distinctly claims the subject matter regarded as the invention.
IV. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. " 102 & 103

Claims 38-41 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2018/0281963 to Dowty ("Dowty"). Claims 24-36 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dowty in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0248655 to Kroll ("Kroll"). Claim 37 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dowty in view of Kroll, and, in the alternative, further in view of U.S. Patent No. 5,024,398 to Riedinger ("Riedinger"). Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration as explained below.
A. Claim 24 is allowable

Applicant respectfully submits that Dowty and Kroll fail to teach or suggest at least the "front side of the storage unit may provide access to the holders of the storage unit" and that the back side of the storage unit is "located against the interior face of the privacy shell" as recited in claim 24. A technical effect of this is that the storage unit may be accessed by a passenger situated inside the passenger seat unit. This has the advantage of the storage unit providing a private storage unit for the passenger (see page 1 lines 20 and 21 of the application as filed).

Referring to the figure below, the Office Action cites to Dowty as allegedly teaching a seat, a privacy shell (combination of aft panel 2510, forward cabin monument 2504, edge 2506 of the forward cabin monument 2504, and aisle-side privacy panel 2508) having an opening (covered by door assembly 2503 and filler door 2509) to allow entry and exit from the seat, a door (2609), and a storage unit (edge 2506 of the forward cabin monument 2504). Office Action page 7. The Office Action concedes that the alleged storage unit (edge 2506 of the forward cabin monument 2504) lacks one or more holders and cites to Kroll to cure this deficiency. Id.
At the outset, Applicant submits that the edge 2506 cannot be a "storage unit" as claimed at least because the edge 2506 lacks both "a back side located against an interior face of the
privacy shell" and "a front side" which "provides access to the holders of the storage unit." The edge 2506 is simply a side of the forward monument 2504.
Applicant further submits that even if the entire forward monument 2504 (of which edge 2506 is a component) were considered a storage unit, it would still not be a storage unit as claimed.

In particular, Applicant respectfully submits that the forward monument 2504 cannot be both the "privacy shell" and the "storage unit" at least because the claim requires that the storage unit include "a back side located against an interior face of the privacy shell." Thus, when properly considered, of the Office Action's grouping of components, the privacy shell at best could only be the combination of the aft panel 2510 and the aisle-side privacy panel 2508. But as illustrated in Fig. 25A above, for example, the forward monument 2504 lacks "a back side located against an interior face of the privacy shell" as recited in claim 24. This is further illustrated in annotated Fig. 26E provided by the Office Action and reproduced below, where a back side or rear end of the storage unit is not located against any component, let alone "an interior face of the privacy shell." For at least these reasons, claim 24 is allowable.

Such positioning of the forward cabin monument of Dowty is consistent with Dowty's teachings that the "forward cabin monument" may be one of "various types of cabin furniture such as storage compartments" (paragraph [0003]) and with "aisle-side doors or openings"

(paragraph [0135]). Nowhere does Dowty teach or suggest that that the entrance to the cabin monument may be anywhere other than on the aisle-side wall of the monument. This differs from the claimed invention in that the storage compartment is accessed from the exterior of the passenger suite, rather than the interior.

For at least these reasons, Dowty fails to teach or suggest a "storage unit" as claimed. The remaining art of record fails to cure this deficiency. Withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
B. Claim 38 is allowable

Applicant respectfully submits that Dowty fails to teach or suggest at least "a privacy shell at least partially surrounding the seat, the privacy shell having a primary opening defining a first and second edge to allow entry to and exit from the seat unit" and a door "arranged to move between the first and second positions in a direction offset by an angle from the first edge of the primary opening of the privacy shell" "wherein the first edge is adjacent to the door when the door is in the second position" and "the door is arranged to slide between the first position and the second position in a direction along a length of the door" as recited in claim 38.
The Office Action alleges that Dowty teaches a privacy shell and a door as illustrated below. Office Action pages 4-5.

However, as illustrated in Fig. 26 of Dowty, for example, the alleged door movement is only offset relative to an interior face of the seat unit, but the door movement is not offset relative to the edge of a primary opening to which the door is adjacent when in the second position. Moreover, the alleged door of Dowty is not "arranged to slide between the first position and the second position in a direction along a length of the door." For at least these reasons, claim 38 is allowable over Dowty.
C. The dependent claims are allowable

Applicant respectfully submits that the remaining claims are allowable at least because they depend from claim 24 or 38 and may be allowable for additional reasons. Withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
